title: Quantization NaN debug scratchpad (INT8/FP8/BF16)
content:
Goal: track commands tried, error snippets, quick hypotheses and repro notes for NaNs observed with INT8/FP8/BF16 quantized variants. Working notes - messy.

Summary of problem:
- Intermittent NaNs during generation on a 7B decoder-only model after switching from bf16->fp8/int8 quantized kernels. Most frequent on long-context (>1024 tokens) streaming workloads.
- NaNs appear after a few hundred tokens; sometimes immediately on first token for some prompts.
- Reproducible locally on CUDA A100 (driver 535) and on Dedicated nodes (same CUDA).

Quick reproducer (what I run locally):
- export MODEL_PATH=/mnt/models/redwood-7b-v2
- python -m serving_runtime.run_infer --model $MODEL_PATH --quantize int8 --dtype fp8 --context 2048 --prompt test_long_prompt.txt --batch 1

Observed stderr (abridged):
- RuntimeWarning: Tensor contains NaN at decoder/layer_10/attn_output (kernel fused_attn.cu:214)
- RuntimeError: kernel launch failed: device-side assert triggered
- Generation output: "... 3.1415 NaN NaN NaN" and then model stops streaming

Commands / experiments tried (chronological):
1) Baseline: run non-quantized bf16 -> no NaNs, long runs stable.
2) FP8 only (no int8): intermittent NaNs. Variation by random seed.
3) INT8 symmetric quantization on weights + fp16 activations: more NaNs than FP8.
4) INT8 with per-channel scales (symmetric) -> slight improvement but NaNs still present for long context.
5) Disabled KV cache (--no-kv-cache): NaNs disappeared in 90% of runs -> strong signal KV cache interaction.
6) Force warmup of KV cache with dummy tokens before real prompt (100 tokens) -> reduces frequency but not eliminated.
7) Clamp activations before softmax (torch.clamp(x, -50, 50)) in attention kernel stub -> NaNs eliminated in that run. But this is a bandaid and changes output.
8) Re-run with layernorm fallback to fp32 (cast LN weights/activations to fp32) -> no NaNs observed across several prompts.

Hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: Accumulation overflow in FP8 path when summing large attention logits for long contexts -> leads to Inf -> downstream NaN after softmax. Explains clamp fix and fp32 layernorm fix.
- Hypothesis B: KV cache indexing / memory corruption when using quantized compressed keys (packed int8/FP8 arrays) -> occasional out-of-bounds write. Explains why disabling KV cache helps.
- Hypothesis C: LayerNorm quantization scale mismatch (scale granularity) leads to denorms or division by near-zero -> NaN in normalized activations. Explains why casting LN to fp32 resolves issue.

Quick checks to run next (ordered):
- Add deterministic check to capture first NaN tensor: run with torch.set_printoptions(threshold=2000) and add checks after every major op: if torch.isnan(x).any(): dump tensor x to /tmp/nan-dumps with op name and callstack.
- Reproduce with small script that toggles only KV cache on/off and isolates attention module. If NaN appears only when KV cache used and not with direct attention -> KV cache packing bug likely.
- Insert assert that KV cache buffer offsets are within expected range before write.
- Try different FP8 exponent/format settings (E4M3 vs E5M2). E4M3 (smaller exponent) gave more NaNs in my quick run.
- Re-quantize layernorm weights per-tensor vs per-channel and run A/B.

Notes about kernels and code paths to inspect:
- serving_runtime/ops/quantized_attn.cu: fused attention uses fp8 reductions and a custom softmax. Suspect reduction path.
- serving_runtime/kv_cache/packed_kv_store.cu: pack/unpack routines for FP8 and INT8. Look for index arithmetic and alignment when sequence length > 1024.
- model conversion pipeline: quantize_weights.py (per-channel scales) -> outputs .q8 files. Verify that .q8 header contains correct zero_point and scale bytes for each layernorm/linear.

Quick local command snippets I used to check tensors (python):
- torch.isnan(x).nonzero()[:10]  # inspect positions
- torch.isinf(x).any(), torch.isfinite(x).all()
- (x.abs() > 1e4).nonzero()  # detect overflow

Repro notes and mitigations tried so far:
- Casting layernorm to fp32 prevents NaNs (good mitigation for production but slower).
- Clamping logits/attention scores prevents immediate Inf but masked outputs degrade quality.
- Changing FP8 format from E4M3 -> E5M2 reduced NaN occurrences in long context tests (consistent across 5 seeds). Suspect exponent range issue.

Potential next steps for production rollouts:
- Short-term: revert to BF16 quantized profiles for long-context customers or enable layernorm-fp32 fallback behind config flag. Update rollout policy so canary to 5% while monitoring. (INF-3421 ticket).
- Medium-term: add KV cache bounds checks and regression tests that simulate 4k+ context with quantized KV and randomized prompts. Add nightly test that runs through few long prompt seeds.
- Long-term: redesign quantized reduction in fused_attn to use chunked accumulation in fp32 before downcast, or implement stochastic rounding to reduce overflow.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- [ ] Add detailed dump of header from .q8 files for layers 8-12 and compare scales to baseline.
- [ ] Add unit test for pack/unpack that writes random kv, reads back, and validates with bitwise checks.
- [ ] Sync with Lee on fused_attn PR (PR #412) to see if recent changes correlate.
- [ ] Add Slack summary for #serving-runtime with short repro and mitigation options.

Breadcrumbs: chat logs and earlier notes indicate this flaked last sprint (Mar 2026) but was not elevated. See ticket INF-3421 and PR #412. I'll update INF-3421 with latest dump and a small repro script.

If stuck: ping @Lee Chen for help on CUDA debugging and @Alex Rivera for model conversion/scale maths.

End of scratchpad.
